CaveGrassSettings: Nested Grass Settings on Room Content Rules of Content Type Grass. Controls blade density, dimensions and independent variation, per-rule blade cap, player-relative Game draw distance, bend radius and material. Snapshotted independently at rebuild; use the rule Enabled, Room Percentage and Seed Salt for population control. Prefab placement controls do not apply.
CaveGrass: Grass Room Content Rule visual layer generated after prefab rules during rebuild. Set CaveRoomContentRule Content Type to Grass; prefab-only controls are hidden and no prefab is required. Nested Grass Settings include Grass Room Percentage (0–100, current profile 35%, default 0), Grass Blades Per Square Metre (0–48, default 18), Grass Height (0.3–2.5 m, default 1.2), Height Variation (0–0.85, default 0.55), Width (0.02–0.25 m, default 0.1), Width Variation (0–0.85, default 0.65), Maximum Blades (0–120000, default 60000), Draw Distance (8–80 m, default 32), Bend Radius (0.3–3 m, default 1.1) and Grass Material. Each rule has an independent seedSalt; multiple Grass rules are allowed, their budgets sum and overlapping coverage may overlap. Samples reject occupied areas independent of prefab rule order. Existing GPU meshes, rounded caps, camera-relative culling and transient player wake are unchanged. Zero percentage, zero density or a missing material disables a rule.
CartoonCharacterGait: Distance-driven procedural locomotion for the knight. It blends twelve style weights into limb IK, body motion, spine pose and Footstep events; actual horizontal travel, rather than time, advances phase. Keep limb references and dimensions consistent with ShadowKnightProportions. Tune step lengths in metres and visual amplitudes in metres/degrees, then test against walls because blocked travel must produce no footsteps.
CaveBody: Configures a fallen knight placed by ProceduralCave. Its seed makes the body proportions and attached torch repeatable. It is generated content: change the source prefab or cave population settings, never a generated instance. Ensure its body and torch references remain intact so the corpse torch can still enter the usual pickup flow.
CaveBoulder: Runtime physical rock produced by a rockfall. It detects player contact while falling, becomes a blocker after landing and can be carried only once settled. TorchInteraction owns carry/drop calls and preserves collision safety during handoff. Boulder tuning comes from CaveGenerationProfile rockfall values, while this component deliberately has no author-facing serialized parameters.
CaveExit: Runtime entrance-exit controller added for the generated cave. It arms only after the player leaves the entrance, respects pickup priority and opens a paused completion summary on return. It restores its previous time scale when disabled. It has no inspector tuning; adjust exit placement/radius through ProceduralCave and verify nearby pickups still win selection.
CaveGenerationProfile: Reusable snapshot for a complete cave rebuild: layout, rocks, traps, built-in populations, elevation, materials and generic room rules. ProceduralCave snapshots Settings at Rebuild start, so changing the asset requires a new rebuild. Player binding stays scene-local. Use profile capture/assignment tools to migrate local values and preserve a seed while comparing layout or population changes. Room Radius accepts 4–32 metres before Room Size Variation: 16 gives four times the area of radius 8, while 32 gives four times its diameter. Layout spacing scales with radius; large radii and many rooms increase mesh size and rebuild time. Existing profiles retain their values. Enable Use Room Radius Range to replace legacy radius/variation with Minimum Room Radius and Maximum Room Radius (2.5–32 metres). Bounds describe base radii before irregularity; equal bounds give equal sizes, one room uses the midpoint, and multiple rooms use seeded stratified samples. Reversed bounds raise maximum to minimum. Range mode spaces rooms using maximum radius and is disabled by default for compatibility. Corridor Length Variation (0–1) adds seeded broad detours between rooms, independently of Corridor Winding; it is not an exact length range. Branch Density zero disables side branches. Minimum/Maximum Branch Length (2–64 m, default 7–12) controls straight-line reach; winding and overlaps affect walked/visible length. Allow Nested Branches lets branches start from earlier branches. Defaults preserve old layouts; the entrance remains separately controlled. Branch Connection Percentage (0–100, default 0) adds tip-to-segment links between different branch families within Branch Connection Distance (2–64 m, default 16). Nested descendants inherit their root family. Nearest eligible segments are selected; already-overlapping tips and duplicate pairs need no extra links. Links are additional to Branch Density, use a separate seeded stream, and exclude the entrance. Set 100 to attempt every tip; a nearby different family is still required. Room Spacing Multiplier (0.25–2, default 1) scales room-centre spacing without changing room radii. Lower values shorten gaps and can merge rooms; branch reach and entrance length remain independently configured. One preserves the previous layout.
CaveRockfallTrap: One-shot corridor hazard built by the cave generator. It warns, releases boulders over its collapse interval, emits pebbles and cleans up owned runtime resources. Leaving after trigger does not cancel it. Its timings, debris sizes and boulder radii are authored through CaveGenerationProfile; do not expose or depend on its internal fall plan.
CaveRoomContentRule: Serializable rule for optional room content after legacy populations have been placed. contentType selects Prefabs, Grass or Water. Prefab rules use the existing prefab, footprint, clearance, wall and alignment settings; Grass rules use nested grass settings, need no prefab and hide prefab-only controls. A stable seedSalt provides an independent random stream. Grass executes after all prefab rules to reject occupied areas independent of rule order; multiple Grass rules are allowed, their budgets sum and overlapping coverage may overlap. Legacy capture migrates old profile grass into a Tall grass rule with seed salt 982451653, preserving exact placement, dimensions and material; later capture preserves the cloned rule including nested grass settings. Existing prefab examples remain Stone Pillars (salt 47021) and Ancient Roots (salt 47022). Water rules use nested width/height/depth/material settings and the seeded floor-placement stream, always upright. Footprints reserve at least the water and ripple radius. No prefab or wall attachment is used. The default Falling Water entry now uses Prefabs with Falling Water.prefab (5 m tall); its component controls appearance. Keep that rule upright with no wall attachment and reserve its footprint manually.
CentipedeBalanceProfile: Shared behaviour balance for centipedes: hunting speed/range, variation, recovery, light response and attack timing. Shape, materials, random seed, target and environment mask remain per creature. Capture from or apply to a centipede through the profile inspector/context action. Preserve a fixed seed and test shadow edges and surface transitions when changing speed or exposure thresholds.
CentipedeLegAudio: Consumes ProceduralCentipede LegStep events through a pooled set of AudioSources. Hearing distance, full-volume distance, audible-leg cap and per-frame step cap control density; the listener is usually the overhead camera. Tune volume/pitch and mixer routing on Centipede.prefab, then test a populated cave so clicks remain readable without flooding the mix.
CharacterDeath: Listens to health death, delays defeat using unscaled time, disables controls and displays the inventory defeat summary. It owns and restores the time scale it pauses. Death delay belongs to PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile when assigned; otherwise the local fallback applies. Test only with a full player component group so profile assignment and summary ownership stay coherent.
CharacterFollowCamera: Simple smoothed camera follow for the movement/cave scenes. It needs a target Transform and an offset; it does not perform obstacle avoidance. Orbit Angle (-180 to 180 degrees) rotates the offset around the target on the world vertical axis, independently of character facing. Zero preserves the original view; the destination keeps offset height and distance. Follow smoothing also smooths movement to the new orbit position, while aiming uses the rotated offset. Camera-relative movement reads the assigned movement camera elsewhere, so keeping the camera target and player relationship valid matters for controls as well as framing. Rockfall impulses add decaying position noise after follow; the previous offset is removed before smoothing to prevent drift. Disabling restores the unshaken position. Simultaneous impulses refresh a bounded displacement amplitude instead of summing. Every accepted Shake call also adds a random signed orbit step: Shake Orbit Degrees is the non-negative min/max magnitude (default 2–5 degrees), with Shake Orbit Smooth Time (default 0.4 s) smoothing toward the accumulated destination. Set both magnitudes to zero to disable new orbit steps. Runtime orbit changes persist after shake fades, stay separate from authored Orbit Angle and use an independent random stream. Repeated shakes retain pending steps; angle wrapping takes the shortest path. Disabling stops the pending orbit transition at its current angle. Damage Shake Amplitude (0.18 metres), Damage Shake Duration (0.3 seconds), and Damage Shake Frequency (24) control a shake on every accepted health hit, including fatal hits. Health is resolved from Target or its parent; rejected damage never shakes. Zero amplitude or duration disables damage shake. Uses the existing bounded Shake impulse and Shake Orbit settings, so hits may also accumulate orbit steps. Disable unsubscribes and removes the transient shake offset; changing Target rebinds health on the next camera update.
CharacterHealth: Slot-based health with time-based refill and a generated HUD. Damage removes a slot, fires Died at zero and updates the display. Slot count and refill seconds can come from PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile; HUD colours and presentation stay local. Test damage, refill and completion/defeat transitions after changing slot count because runtime slot views are rebuilt from the effective value.
CharacterInventory: Session-only inventory that groups collected Treasure by effective display name and unit value, counts coins through Treasure.IsCoin and presents collection/exit/defeat summaries. It can use scene-authored TMP UI or create a fallback canvas. Keep UI under the source UI canvas and preserve the render-texture composition; it does not save across sessions.
CharacterKnockdown: Applies the low-pose knockdown sequence, temporary immunity and movement-gated recovery. Recovery cannot advance merely by waiting: ReportMovement must receive real travel. Its durations and immunity can be shared through PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile. It also causes the held torch to drop, so test recovery with a torch and a centipede/trap hit.
CharacterStress: Tracks encounter and hit stress, recovery delay and a visual hunch/head-noise response. It uses nearby threat encounters rather than a global story state. PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile can centralize numeric stress values; hunch angle, head look and motion chaos remain local presentation. Test encounter reset and recovery with realistic creature ranges. Darkness adds Darkness Stress Per Second × shared PlayerLightExposure.Darkness each second (default 5 at full darkness); active darkness delays recovery. Configure the rate in the assigned player balance profile, or local fallback without a profile. A missing/disabled light probe adds no stress. Returning to light stops this gain but does not clear accumulated stress; existing Recovery Per Second and Recovery Delay still apply.
CrawlSurfaceMesh: Read-only acceleration structure for centipede ray queries against visible cave surfaces when collision geometry differs. ProceduralCentipede rebuilds caches when cave meshes regenerate. It is not an Inspector-authored object and exposes no tuning values. If traversal fails after a cave material/mesh change, verify collider/surface availability and the creature environment mask instead.
DitherAccentRendererFeature: URP Render Graph feature that gathers dither accents, selected pickup outlines and optional occluded-player masks before compositing through OneBitDither. Both passes run before URP post-processing, in mask-then-dither enqueue order. Enable Post Processing on the world camera and assign a Volume profile on a layer included by its Volume Mask; effects process the dithered image and can soften its pattern or change its palette. It requires the project renderer assets and compatible materials. Do not add the old Full Screen Pass alongside it. Rendering parameters are asset/material settings; selected targets come from gameplay registries each frame. Living shadows are evaluated before tone quantization, using per-camera held-player torch position and fuel. Four outward color samples extend dark regions into a configurable number of noise-bent fingers. No effect in Edit Mode, without a held player torch, or on the player mask/UI. Tune Living Shadows, Shadow Reach At Low Fuel (metres), Shadow Tendril Width, Shadow Motion Speed and Shadow Player Safe Radius on OneBitDither.mat. This is a screen-space approximation, not gameplay illumination. Shadow Count In Bright Light (default 4) and Shadow Count In Dim Light (default 12) accept 1–24; the effective dim count is never below the bright count. Count follows the held torch burnout light envelope, not flicker or measured screen area. Fixed golden-angle directions fade new fingers in continuously. Equal counts give a fixed count; visible fingers also require darkness in their direction. Outward samples must match the expected world position: confidence fades over 0.08–0.35 metres of depth-reconstructed position error. Background, off-screen samples and discontinuities stop the sample chain so rock silhouettes cannot seed stretched shadows on another surface. Steep surfaces can suppress fingers; attachment remains a screen-space approximation. Transparent opt-in DitherAccent materials are composited after opaque accents in back-to-front order against the same scene depth; falling cave water uses this path.
FootstepAudio: Plays left/right gait footstep events through two runtime sources positioned at contact feet. Blended gait weights determine sneak/walk/run volume and pitch, while a minimum interval prevents bursts. Tune clips, mixer group and distances on the knight prefab. Since gait events are distance-based, validate starts, stops and wall collisions rather than testing only animation speed.
GaitStylePose: Runtime value type describing the combined stride, bounce, arm and spine pose for one gait style. CartoonCharacterGait evaluates and blends it; ProceduralSpine consumes the result. Its public members are transient pose data, not designer Inspector fields. Extend it only with matching evaluation and application logic, then verify every style blend.
HandheldTorch: Owns torch light, world-space fire/smoke, holding pose, fuel age, burn-out and physical dropping. Fuel persists across pickup, dropping and disable/re-enable; strikes and drops add configured lifetime cost. Illumination/fuel can use TorchBalanceProfile, but particle refs, colour and pose remain local. Its execution order is 100, before attack and interaction overlays. Water contact permanently extinguishes the instance for the session after final pose overlays: light and particles stop immediately, and pickup/drop/disable cannot relight it. Checks sweep the flame position with an 8 cm radius, not the player or handle.
MusicPlayer: Creates and fades a looping music AudioSource with assigned clip and mixer group. Fade durations use runtime update state and are independent of gameplay balance profiles. Use it for scene ambience, preserve mixer routing and avoid attaching competing music players unless intentional. Validate fade-in/out in the target scene because time-scale behavior is part of the scene loop.
PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile: Shared player balance asset grouping movement, health, stress, knockdown, attack, interaction and death. Capture/apply requires all seven player components and assignment is atomic; missing components leave state unchanged. Local fields remain exact fallback when no asset is assigned. Profile controls numeric gameplay values, not rig references, colours or attack pose angles.
PlayerOcclusionOutline: Opt-in player silhouette data for DitherAccentRendererFeature. It records the camera, mask material, outline colour and pixel width, then caches child renderers. Use it only where occlusion readability is needed, such as ProceduralCave. Call RefreshRenderers after changing nested meshes/material slots; transparent geometry without depth writes cannot occlude the silhouette.
PoseEasing: Internal mathematical easing helpers used by attack and interaction poses. It has no scene setup or Inspector parameters. Designers tune the caller durations and angles; code changes here affect multiple gestures at once, so preserve continuity and verify handoff between gait, torch, attack and interaction overlays.
ProceduralCave: Primary cave orchestrator. It generates connected rooms, mesh/collision, entrance/exit, rocks, rockfalls, residents, bodies, treasure and coins, then replaces the disposable generated root on rebuild. Use CaveGenerationProfile for reusable authoring and preserve seed independence between content streams. The default profile uses the Dark Stone wall material. Procedural Cave Wall Crawlers remains available as an optional material using the Cave Crawlers Lit shader; its main Lit pass draws world-space crawler silhouettes directly on the material without extra crawler objects or a separate accent draw. Cells Per Metre supports 0.2-64; at high density, effective crawler size and wiggle are capped by cell size to prevent clipping at constant per-pixel cost. Generated children are not durable edit targets; test fixed-seed traversal and placement after changes.
ProceduralCentipede: Builds a disposable segmented rig and performs local surface-relative stalking, fleeing, hiding and attacks. Gameplay light exposure is collider-occluded sampling, not rendered pixels; directional moonlight is ignored. It needs valid traversable colliders in Environment Mask and a target. Profile shared behaviour while keeping shape/seed/mask local, then test interior boundaries and recovery.
ProceduralCharacter: Reads Rewired or Input System movement, moves the CharacterController camera-relatively and feeds actual velocity/distance to gait. Stick magnitude chooses Sneak/Walk; held Run overrides styles. PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile supplies thresholds and speeds, while camera/rig references remain local. Test keyboard and stick fallback paths plus interactions because movement stays active during gestures.
ProceduralSpine: Deforms the torso mesh and named spine joints from the current blended gait pose. It creates an instance deformation mesh while retaining the source mesh. Bend/twist/side-bend multipliers and response time are local visual controls, not profile balance. Keep the named knight hierarchy stable and validate torch/attack chest overlays after proportion changes.
ShadowKnightProportions: Execute-always root rig authoring for limb lengths, torso dimensions, head size, arm spread and helmet visibility. It updates named transforms, gait dimensions, spine setup and torch grip relationships. Use its custom Inspector outside Play Mode and preserve part names. Large proportion changes require checking attack angles, reach, capsule fit and procedural mesh appearance.
TorchAttack: Held attack controller: press winds up, release strikes, then recovers while movement continues. It spends torch strike fuel and overlays right arm/optional chest after the torch hold pose. Timing comes from PlayerGameplayBalanceProfile; pose angles remain local to the knight rig. Its execution order is 150, so update suppression every frame and test fuel plus return-to-hold.
TorchBalanceProfile: Shared Torch profile with illumination (brightness/range) and fuel (lifetime, burnout fraction, strike/drop cost) groups. Apply it to HandheldTorch through its inspector/context action; null keeps local fields. It intentionally excludes colour, flicker, particles and grip pose, allowing scene/prefab visuals to vary while the gameplay light economy stays consistent.
TorchInteraction: Selects the nearest reachable treasure first, then a free ground torch, settled boulder and eligible exit. It drives reach/crouch overlays and rechecks range and obstruction at transfer; E never replaces or drops a held torch. Player profile supplies pickup timing/range, while carry placement/prompt remain local. Its execution order is 175.
Treasure: Collectible runtime identity, illumination sampling, glint handling and distance-size behavior. A TreasureDefinition overrides legacy name/value/category when assigned; SetValue is per-instance only. Active registries include generated items, enabling pickup selection after rebuilds. Tune visibility/glints locally and economy through definitions, then verify light gating and inventory grouping.
TreasureDefinition: ScriptableObject holding durable player-facing display name, unit value and coin category independently of prefab naming. Inventory groups by its effective name/value and summary coin count uses IsCoin. Create or duplicate definitions under Gameplay/Treasures and assign one per variant; capture from a Treasure records current effective values without mutating shared assets at runtime.
UiRenderTexture: Owns the transient UI camera RenderTexture and writes it to the presentation RawImage at current screen resolution. Its depth/stencil target preserves ScrollRect masking. Keep source interactive UI under the source canvas; the output canvas only composites it after world effects. It recreates targets after size changes and releases them on disable.
CaveRockfallFeedback: Add to the persistent ProceduralCave object to configure presentation for all generated traps. Collapse Clips selects one non-empty entry randomly and plays it once at collapse start with an independent random Pitch Range (default 0.85–1.15), spatial attenuation, Volume and optional mixer Output. Shake Enabled, Collapse/Landing Amplitude, Duration and Frequency control bounded follow-camera impulses. Distance is measured from the player: full strength through Shake Full Distance, then linear falloff to Shake Max Distance. Each boulder sends only its first natural landing; carrying/dropping does not replay it. Follow Camera defaults to Camera.main. Settings stay on the scene generator and are not part of CaveGenerationProfile.
DarknessWhisperAudio: ProceduralCave / Darkness Whispers plays the assigned whisper loop in 2D, starting at zero volume. Player and Sample Offset locate the light probe. Point/spot light contributions use intensity × squared range falloff, culling masks and collider occlusion for shadow-casting lights; player and emitter colliders are ignored. Ambient/directional moonlight and screen-space effects are ignored, matching creature gameplay. Volume is Maximum Volume × (1 − clamp01(exposure / Silent Exposure)); defaults: maximum 1, silence at exposure 3, full-range fade 3 seconds. Other nearby torches contribute, including dropped torches. Environment Mask selects occluders. AudioSource mixer routing is preserved. Disabling stops playback; enabling restarts silently. Missing Player keeps audio silent. In ProceduralCave an assigned PlayerLightExposure now supplies the shared light measurement and darkness threshold; legacy probe fields are only used without an active shared probe. Maximum Volume is preserved.
PlayerLightExposure: Shared player light probe, evaluated before stress. Sample Offset defaults to (0,1,0); Fully Lit Exposure defaults to 3; Environment Mask selects occluders. Darkness = 1 - clamp01(exposure / threshold). Point/spot light uses squared range attenuation and collider occlusion; ambient/directional light is ignored. Supplies both stress and whispers.
CharacterBreathingAudio: Dedicated Player Breathing object in ProceduralCave loops Breath.wav in 2D. CharacterStress 0–100 maps from Minimum Playback Speed (1) to Maximum Playback Speed (1.6), smoothed by Pitch Response Time (0.15 seconds). Playback speed also changes pitch. Volume (0.5) is independent; Fade In Duration is 0.2 seconds. Missing/disabled stress uses calm speed. Disable stops; enable restarts. Preserve AudioSource mixer routing. Running Playback Multiplier (1.3) multiplies stress-driven speed while Run is held and actual movement exceeds 0.05 m/s. Character defaults to the stress object. Standing still or pushing into a wall stops the multiplier; pitch smoothly returns to the stress-driven rate. Unity pitch caps the combined result at 3.
CharacterDarknessDamage: On Shadow Knight in ProceduralCave, holding an active burned-out HandheldTorch in full darkness (PlayerLightExposure.Exposure <= Full Darkness Exposure, default 0.0001) accumulates a scaled timer. Roll Interval (5 seconds) attempts one independent X-in-6 roll (default X=1): roll d6 and succeed on 1 through X. X=3 is 50%, X=0 never succeeds, X=6 always succeeds; the shared Dice.RollXIn6 helper takes a caller-owned random stream; success consumes one existing health segment via TryTakeDamage and registers hit stress. Empty hands, a burning torch, light, death, completed run or disabled/missing probe prevent damage and reset the timer. Torch lookup refreshes every Torch Refresh Interval (1 second); current ownership is checked every tick. Disable resets the timer. Long frames perform at most one roll, without a damage burst. No forced knockdown or torch drop.
CharacterDamageAudio: Dedicated Player Damage Audio object references CharacterHealth. Injury Clips and Death Clips start empty for designer assignment; null entries are ignored. Accepted nonlethal damage picks one injury clip; fatal damage picks only one death clip and stops ongoing injury audio. Each list has separate volume and minimum/maximum pitch (0.9–1.1). Random selection is independent of gameplay random streams. 2D AudioSource preserves mixer routing; death audio continues at timeScale zero. Disabled component unsubscribes and stops its source. Re-enabling does not replay an already handled death.
CaveWater: Reusable falling-water component on Assets/Prefabs/Falling Water.prefab. The default Falling Water room-content rule uses Content Type Prefabs and this asset. Edit the prefab component for width (0.8 m), height (5 m, doubled from 2.5 m), depth (0.35 m) and shared material; rebuild the cave afterward. Keep rule Align To Floor off, wall placement at zero and footprint large enough for the stream and ripples. A 6-triangle mesh is regenerated on enable, including directly placed prefab instances. Two crossing ribbons and floor ripples share a procedural URP material with DitherAccent; no particles, simulation, refraction or extra lights. Swept flame contact after pose overlays extinguishes the torch for the session. Missing material disables contact. Legacy procedural Water rules remain supported.
CaveWaterSettings: Legacy nested settings for Content Type Water: shared material, full width/depth and height above the floor. Missing material disables procedural generation and its wet hazard. Rules snapshot and validate their nested settings independently. The default Falling Water rule now uses Content Type Prefabs, so edit CaveWater on Falling Water.prefab instead of these nested settings.
CharacterDepthOfField: Attach to the world camera and assign Target and the existing Global Volume. Runs after camera follow, orbit and shake. Gaussian Start follows target view-axis depth plus Sharp Margin (2 metres); End adds Blur Range (6 metres). Runtime changes use the Volume profile instance and restore thresholds when disabled. Keep Gaussian mode, radius 1.2 and high-quality sampling in the profile. PC/Mobile renderer PostProcessData uses the project Gaussian shader with orthographic linear-depth conversion; perspective conversion remains unchanged. Blur only affects background depth, not distance sideways from the character. Other effects in the same Volume remain authored settings.
